brief.hq: Somerville, Massachusetts (factory in Weirton, West Virginia)
brief.ticker: Private ($750M Series G, Aug 2026; $1.75B pre-money reported)
brief.deck: Form Energy, the Somerville iron-air battery maker building Google's 30 GWh, 100-hour system in Minnesota, closed a $750M Series G led by T. Rowe Price on 12 August 2026, taking total equity past $2B as its announced backlog jumped from roughly 20 GWh to 80 GWh.
brief.the_case_p1: Form announced the $750M Series G on 12 August, led by T. Rowe Price, with Sequoia Capital, Janus Henderson, Franklin Templeton and PEAK6 new to the register. Total equity passes $2B; proceeds scale Form Factory 1 in Weirton, West Virginia. Axios reports the round priced at $1.75B pre-money, down from about $3B in October 2024. The order book explains the investors' patience: an announced backlog of 80 GWh, led by the 300 MW / 30 GWh Google and Xcel Energy system in Minnesota, and 12 GWh for Crusoe's AI data centres.
brief.the_case_p2: Weirton is the story a sponsor buys: a 550,000-square-foot battery plant on a former steel-mill site, around 400 people and a planned 500 MW a year by 2028, shipping 100-hour batteries to utilities and hyperscalers. Axios and TechCrunch report a listing being prepared for 2027. A down round is a reason to build the brand, not to hide: the next four quarters decide whether Form is priced as a manufacturer or a technology bet.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The Series G closed on 12 August, and a reported 2027 listing puts brand-building inside the next four quarters. Formula E's GEN4 era opens in Jeddah on 18 December; the new Austin E-Prix on 6 February 2027 and Miami on 20 February give an American storage brand two home rounds before any roadshow.
brief.why_team_para: Andretti is the American team on the grid, run from Indianapolis; parent TWG Motorsports also operates the Cadillac F1 team. The roster is TWG AI, Quest Global, Crowe UK and Reflo; the sponsor table shows no energy or storage brand, so the lane is open. Google Cloud is the championship's technology partner and Google is Form's anchor customer: the ecosystem already overlaps. For a utility-and-hyperscaler brand, an American car at Austin and Miami is the right stage.
brief.value_content: MODE B - halo, said plainly: a 100-hour iron-air battery has no race-day role. The mechanics are commercial. Official Energy Storage Partner status and sidepod placement on the American car; Austin and Miami hospitality for utility executives, regulators and hyperscaler energy buyers; Weirton factory content pairing a steel-town rebuild with the team's GEN4 debut; and pre-listing visibility to the capital-markets audience already in the Formula E paddock.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Energy Storage Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, Seasons 13-15 (2026/27 to 2028/29), bridging the reported 2027 listing and the first Google and Crusoe deliveries. Estimated $1.5-2.5M a year. Scope: sidepod branding, Austin and Miami hospitality, factory and grid content, driver visits to Weirton, and a utility-customer programme through TWG Motorsports.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Jaramillo co-founded Form in 2017 after helping launch Tesla's Powerwall and fronts every raise. Path: Ted Wiley, Co-Founder, President and COO; Navneet Govil, CFO, formerly of SoftBank Investment Advisers; Wes Sloan, incoming COO from Panasonic Energy. No chief marketing officer is listed.
brief.opening_angle_intro: Lead with Weirton and the listing.
brief.opening_angle_quote: “Mateo, you have 80 GWh of backlog, a steel-town factory and a listing to price. The American Formula E team races in Austin and Miami in February with an open energy lane. 25 minutes to see what a three-season seat costs?”
score_cells: Round closed 12 Aug; GEN4 opener in December, Austin and Miami in February.
$750M raised, over $2B in total; down round, proceeds go to Weirton.
American reindustrialisation, Google and AI power; strong adjacency.
Reported 2027 listing is the trigger; not company-confirmed.
MODE B: no race-day use; open lane, US rounds, ecosystem overlap.
risks: Series G priced at $1.75B pre-money against about $3B in 2024; proceeds are earmarked for Weirton and deployments.
Price the entry under $3M a year and tie it to the listing narrative the board is already funding.
Iron-air batteries have no role in the garage; value rests on audience, content and timing.
Measure renewal on utility and hyperscaler meetings at Austin and Miami, not on lap time.
brief.bottom_line: $750M closed on 12 August, an 80 GWh order book led by Google and Crusoe, a West Virginia factory and a reported 2027 listing: Form Energy needs a national brand within the year and has the story to carry one. Andretti's energy lane is open and two US E-Prix fall in February.

why_now.label: Trigger
why_now.text: Form Energy announced a $750M Series G on 12 August 2026, led by T. Rowe Price, with Sequoia Capital, Janus Henderson, Franklin Templeton and PEAK6 joining existing investors including Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Coatue, TPG Rise Climate and GE Vernova. Total equity raised now exceeds $2B. The proceeds scale Form Factory 1 in Weirton, West Virginia, and fund commercial deployments.

why_now.label: A down round, read honestly
why_now.text: Axios reports the round priced at $1.75B pre-money, down from about $3B in October 2024. That is a reason to build the brand rather than a reason to pass: the investors who took the lower price are the ones who want the company recognised as an industrial manufacturer before it lists. Axios and TechCrunch report a listing being prepared for 2027; the brief treats that as reported, not confirmed.

why_now.label: The order book
why_now.text: Announced backlog rose from roughly 20 GWh to 80 GWh. The anchor is the 300 MW / 30 GWh Google and Xcel Energy system at Pine Island, Minnesota, announced in February 2026 as the largest battery system by energy capacity yet announced, with TechCrunch reporting Google paid about $1B. Crusoe signed for 12 GWh at CERAWeek in March 2026 for its AI data centres. Deliveries from Weirton begin in 2027.

why_now.label: Calendar window
why_now.text: Formula E's GEN4 era opens with the Jeddah double-header on 18-19 December 2026. The new Austin E-Prix at Circuit of The Americas on 6 February 2027 and the Miami E-Prix on 20 February 2027 put an American brand in front of a US audience twice in a month, before any listing roadshow.

why_team.label: The open lane
why_team.text: Andretti Formula E's roster is TWG AI as primary and AI partner, Quest Global for engineering services, Crowe UK for audit and advisory, Reflo for sustainable sportswear and TWG Motorsports as owner, with Nissan powertrains from Season 13. The sponsor table shows no energy, storage or utility brand on the team: Official Energy Storage Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price.

why_team.label: The American team
why_team.text: Andretti is run from Indianapolis, the only US-owned team on the Formula E grid, and its parent TWG Motorsports also operates the Cadillac Formula 1 team with General Motors. A company whose story is a West Virginia steel town rebuilt around batteries belongs on the American car.

why_team.label: Ecosystem overlap
why_team.text: Google Cloud is the championship's technology partner and Google is Form's anchor customer through the Pine Island system. Crusoe, Form's 12 GWh data-centre customer, is itself courting the grid. The paddock Form would join already contains the customers it sells to.

why_team.label: A story the team can tell
why_team.text: Formula E's on-track narrative is energy management. Form's product stores power for a hundred hours to carry a grid through days without wind or sun. The contrast, a forty-five-minute race against a four-day battery, is a content line the team can run all season without inventing a technical link that does not exist.

value.label: Honest MODE B halo
value.text: An iron-air battery is a grid asset; it will not sit in the garage or power the pit lane. The partnership's value is commercial and should be sold that way: an American storage brand on an American car in a championship built on electrification, in the year before a reported listing.

value.label: Commercial lift for the team
value.text: Form brings the guest list the team's other partners want to meet: utility executives, state regulators, hyperscaler energy buyers and the bankers around a 2027 listing. Hospitality at Austin and Miami, and a utility-customer programme through TWG Motorsports, turn those guests into pipeline for both sides.

value.label: Content and ecosystem
value.text: Factory-floor content from Weirton, driver visits to a steel-town plant, co-produced explainers on multi-day storage against race-day energy recovery, and joint activations with the championship's Google Cloud programme where Formula E allows.

value.label: What the team gives back
value.text: Official Energy Storage Partner designation, sidepod branding, Austin and Miami hospitality, driver and engineering access for Form's channels, and visibility to the capital-markets audience that follows the series.

ruled_out.reason: DS Automobiles leaves Formula E at the end of Season 12 and Penske's Season 13 entry with its own GEN4 powertrain was not yet registered at the last report; TotalEnergies holds the energy lane in any case.

The team's owner, Envision Group, includes the battery maker Envision AESC and the wind and storage business Envision Energy: a storage brand on that car competes with the owner. Paysafe became title partner on 14 August 2026.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Mateo Jaramillo before the Jeddah opener to confirm the Series G terms and the listing timetable on the record, agree an Austin E-Prix announcement window, and size an Official Energy Storage Partner entry at Andretti Formula E for Seasons 13-15.
